CREATE HNSW VECTOR INDEX CSIDX ON MyTable (MyVectorCol)

  SEARCH CONFIGURATION '{"efSearch": 200}'; [sap-hana-vector#98334ffc4534#00]

No — COSINE_SIMILARITY and L2DISTANCE are different similarity measures.

- SAP HANA Cloud provides both L2DISTANCE and COSINE_SIMILARITY as separate built‑in functions (they are two distinct measures) [sap-hana-vector#03ade8a69fa1#00].
- They behave differently in queries: L2DISTANCE is typically used with ORDER BY L2DISTANCE(...) (smaller = more similar), while COSINE_SIMILARITY must be ordered DESC because higher cosine values mean more similar [sap-hana-vector#58f76ab47d73#00].
- COSINE_SIMILARITY divides by vector lengths and therefore can return NULL for all‑zero vectors or in cases of numeric underflow; its numeric behavior differs from L2DISTANCE (and both use single‑precision arithmetic with possible overflow/variation) [sap-hana-vector#d4aed736c06f#00].
- Example values illustrate COSINE_SIMILARITY output (e.g., returns 0.5 for the shown vectors), demonstrating it yields a similarity score rather than a distance magnitude [sap-hana-vector#4d2dd05a786e#00].

answer:
- Vector column types and basic constraint
  - HANA Cloud provides built-in vector data types REAL_VECTOR and HALF_VECTOR for storing embeddings [sap-hana-vector#1a201a9b357f#00].

- What a vector index accelerates
  - A vector index speeds up top‑k nearest‑neighbor (similarity) queries by avoiding a full scan of all vectors: without an index the database must load all vectors from disk and compute similarities for each, while with an index only a small portion of vector data needs to be loaded, greatly reducing query time and CPU usage [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#00][sap-hana-vector#ffcfc7d4aadf#00].
  - Note: vector indexes are approximate (not both exact and fast due to the curse of dimensionality); they typically find very close neighbors but do not guarantee the absolute best results, and index accuracy can be tuned at the cost of build time, memory, and/or query time [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#00][sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#01].

- Supported index type
  - SAP HANA supports the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) index for vector columns [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#01].

- Similarity measures the index can use
  - Vector indexes are built for a particular similarity measure and can only be used for similarity searches that use that same measure; SAP HANA Cloud offers two similarity measures for vectors (the provided context states there are two measures but does not name them) [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#01][sap-hana-vector#1a201a9b357f#00].

- Additional operational constraints and notes
  - You can create multiple vector indexes on the same vector column, but at most one index per similarity measure per column (for example, you may have one cosine index and one L2 index on the same column, but not two cosine indexes) [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#01].
  - Because indexes are approximate, a similarity search result can differ before vs. after index creation; if you require exact results despite an existing index, use the NO_VECTOR_INDEX hint to suppress index usage [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#02].

answer:
- Result-accuracy caveat: HNSW is an approximate nearest-neighbor index and does not guarantee returning the true top-k nearest vectors; similarity searches may yield different results after index creation than before [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#01] [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#02].  
  - The index is built for a specific similarity measure and can only be used for searches using that measure; only one index per (column, similarity measure) is allowed [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#01].

- Costs (resources and time): higher index accuracy typically increases index build time, memory consumption, and/or query times when performing similarity searches [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#01] [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#00].  
  - Build parameters: M and efConstruction control the index. efConstruction has a larger impact on memory consumption than M and configures the neighborhood size considered during build; higher efConstruction increases build time and recall (accuracy) and raises memory use [sap-hana-vector#588f6611e877#00].  
  - Typical memory use: an HNSW index typically consumes fewer than 100 bytes per vector; e.g., for 768‑dimensional vectors the index size should be less than ~5% of the vector column size [sap-hana-vector#588f6611e877#00].

- How to get exact results when an index exists: suppress use of the vector index with the NO_VECTOR_INDEX hint in the query; this forces exact search behavior. If you want to try forcing use of the index, use the VECTOR_INDEX hint (the optimizer may still decide not to use it) [sap-hana-vector#73ccb4a69a23#02] [sap-hana-vector#ab07eabb1276#01].

answer:
- What an embedding is
  - An embedding is a vector representation of text — e.g., an "Embedding vectors of the TEXT column" stored in a REAL_VECTOR column [sap-hana-vector#932d3e63bcbc#02].

- How to generate text embeddings inside SAP HANA Cloud
  - You can create embeddings either with SAP's integrated NLP embedding service or with external embedding services via SAP AI Core. SAP HANA Cloud provides a VECTOR_EMBEDDING scalar function and a CREATE_VECTOR_EMBEDDINGS procedure for this purpose [sap-hana-vector#95295143e0cc#00].
  - Using the CREATE_VECTOR_EMBEDDINGS procedure (mass creation on a table):
    - Add a vector column to the table, for example:
      ALTER TABLE TAB ADD (EMB REAL_VECTOR COMMENT 'Embedding vectors of the TEXT column...'); [sap-hana-vector#932d3e63bcbc#02]
    - Call the procedure to create embeddings for all texts that don't yet have an embedding, for example (NLP example):
      CALL CREATE_VECTOR_EMBEDDINGS(
        SCHEMA_NAME => CURRENT_SCHEMA,
        TABLE_NAME => 'TAB',
        TEXT_COLUMN_NAME => 'TEXT',
        EMBEDDING_COLUMN_NAME => 'EMB',
        TEXT_TYPE => 'DOCUMENT',
        MODEL_AND_VERSION => 'SAP_NEB.20240715'
      ); [sap-hana-vector#932d3e63bcbc#02]
    - If using an external model via SAP AI Core, you must pass the remote source name and the remote model identifier, for example:
      CALL CREATE_VECTOR_EMBEDDINGS(... MODEL_AND_VERSION => 'amazon--titan-embed-text."1.2"', REMOTE_SOURCE_NAME => 'MY_SERVICE_INSTANCE', BATCH_SIZE => 1) [sap-hana-vector#3592dd1da9d8#17]
    - The VECTOR_EMBEDDING function can also be called directly (example shows passing the model and the remote source identifier) [sap-hana-vector#3592dd1da9d8#16].
  - Note: to use HANA's integrated NLP embedding functionality, the NLP service must be enabled in your system [sap-hana-vector#3e58d720c869#00].

answer:
- Pricing model
  - Generative AI usage is measured in GenAI tokens, a virtual unit that represents input and output token usage; the number of processed tokens that corresponds to one GenAI token varies by model [sap-ai-core#2bb424212bcc#01].
  - Tokens are converted into capacity units (based on input and output volume), and billing is calculated according to those capacity units. Costs vary by model type and usage pattern [sap-ai-core#661954ac5bef#00][sap-ai-core#2bb424212bcc#01].
  - The generative AI hub is available only as part of the extended service plan (so hub usage is covered under that offering) [sap-ai-core#661954ac5bef#00].

- Where to view consumption in SAP BTP cockpit
  - In your global account, open Usage from the navigation panel, filter by AI Core, and click Export. The exported report contains generative AI hub model consumption under Applications and resource-group–level consumption under Instance [sap-ai-core#007c58362e6b#00].
  - A detailed consumption report for the Generative AI hub (part of SAP AI Core) in the BTP cockpit shows consumption specific to each LLM model, the orchestration service, and consumption for each resource group [sap-ai-core#66b4a4bbbcf3#16].

(For full pricing details and example calculations, see the Metering and Pricing for Generative AI and Metering and Pricing for Predictive AI documents referenced in the product documentation) [sap-ai-core#0a444c83ee73#00].

answer:
- Create a column table with a vector column constrained to a fixed dimension (here 3):
  CREATE COLUMN TABLE VECTORTAB (ID INT, V REAL_VECTOR(3)); [sap-hana-vector#87abf8363da8#00]

- Insert vector literals by first constructing the vector (no implicit conversions). Example inserts:
  INSERT INTO VECTORTAB VALUES (1, TO_REAL_VECTOR('[2,3,5]'));
  INSERT INTO VECTORTAB VALUES (2, TO_REAL_VECTOR('[7,11,13]')); [sap-hana-vector#90d27ec51150#00]

- Update and delete examples:
  UPDATE VECTORTAB SET V = TO_REAL_VECTOR('[17,19,23]') WHERE ID = 1;
  DELETE FROM VECTORTAB WHERE ID = 2; [sap-hana-vector#90d27ec51150#00]

Notes:
- REAL_VECTOR columns are not supported in row tables; use a column table as shown. [sap-hana-vector#87abf8363da8#00]
- Vectors must be constructed (for example with TO_REAL_VECTOR) before inserting because there are no implicit conversions. [sap-hana-vector#90d27ec51150#00]
